product: commentary — no product (an AI-podcast-ad workflow promo)
hook: "ai podcast ads might be one of the easiest ways to make ugc feel native again" — format claim.
body: Instead of another creator-holding-product, put them behind a microphone — the format reads as content, not an ad; testable variants: solo clips, 2-person conversations, expert explanations, controversial opinions, story-based mentions, reaction/interview; the advantage is iteration — one script becomes 10+ podcast creatives (new creators, hooks, settings, opening lines) without reshooting.
cta: "rt + comment 'podcast' and i'll send it (follow for dm)" (workflow lead magnet).
idea: The podcast frame is a hook-swap multiplier — one script × new creators × new hooks × new settings = 10+ native-feeling creatives with zero reshoots.
formatting: Text post + 71s video; 44 likes, 55 bookmarks, 54 replies — high reply rate.
why_it_works: "Without reshooting anything" is the unlock — it reframes creative volume from a production problem into a remixing problem.
what_to_steal: LC's podcast-clip remix lane: take winning UGC scripts, re-deliver as 2-person podcast clips with swapped hooks — 10 variants per script, no reshoot.

product: commentary — no product (a Demand Gen creative-iteration playbook)
hook: "for anyone looking to crack cold traffic on demand gen" — practitioner-to-practitioner.
body: The iteration framework behind $10–20K/day brand spend: swap the hook (keep the 30–90s body identical, write 5+ new hooks); new lead structures (story, listicle, hype, problem/benefit, misconception, information leads); cut/extend agitation; test video lengths; change closings (proof, guarantee, CTA, urgency, offers); new visuals (split-screen, B-rolls, styles); adapt winning scripts into new formats (UGC, AI animation, podcast, mini VSL, founder story); image angle → video and vice versa; testing structure (1-1-1 for high spend, up to 5 creatives per ad group otherwise; 0.4x–1x target CPA per test per day); then test audiences, markets, offers, funnels, placements on winners.
idea: Creative iteration is a layered system with the hook swap at the top — hook → lead structure → length → closing → visuals → format — each layer cheaper than rebuilding the ad.
sequencing: Layer 1: swap the hook (5+ new hooks, same body)
formatting: Long text post; 57 bookmarks — the folder's playbook post.
why_it_works: Ordering the layers by leverage (hook first, rebuild last) gives teams a decision tree instead of a tip list — it answers "what do I change first" definitively.
what_to_steal: The full layer order for LC's iteration SOP: every dying LC winner gets hook-swap first (5+ hooks, same body), then lead-structure, then the deeper layers — never a from-scratch rebuild.

product: commentary — no product (a copywriter's 3 lessons post)
hook: "3 things I've learned writing and strategizing ads for 8-figure brands" — experience claim.
body: Lesson 1: infinite winning ads — segments (personas, symptoms, situations, desires) × awareness levels × ways to write (hooks, angles, stories, vibes, tones, voices) × creative styles (UGC, VSLs, pixar, claymation, rankings, tiktok love letter) = never run out of ideas. Lesson 2: think like a scroller, not a copywriter — UGC creators out-script copywriters because they know what stops the scroll; write for attention, not to impress writers. Lesson 3: copy is one part — strategists also brief designers, recommend hook visuals, own vibe and tone.
idea: The idea matrix (segments × awareness × writing modes × creative styles) makes "infinite winning ads" a combinatorics problem, not a creativity problem.
sequencing: Lesson 3: copy is one part (brief, visuals, vibe)
The closer (building a winner you directed end-to-end)
why_it_works: The matrix turns creative ideation from inspiration into multiplication — anyone can generate combinations, which democratizes the "infinite ideas" claim.
what_to_steal: LC's idea matrix: jewelry personas × awareness × hooks/angles × formats — run the combinatorics instead of waiting for inspiration; and the "think like a scroller" bar for every hook.

product: commentary — no product (a YouTube creative-testing playbook)
hook: "How I split test creatives on YouTube without wasting budget:" — efficiency promise.
body: The testing rules: separate hooks from bodies BEFORE shooting (hook = first 5s, body = everything after); test hooks against each other on the same body — 10 hooks × 2 bodies = 20 combos from one shoot; launch 3–5 creatives per ad group (not 10); wait 14 days before cutting (week-1 data is noise); cut on spend-vs-CPA (2–3x target CPA with zero conversions = done); check hook retention before conversions (high 5s skip = fix the hook, not the offer); never touch a winner until fatigue signals (rising CPA, falling retention/CTR); produce in batches so 3–5 new hooks are ready when fatigue hits.
idea: Hook/body separation before the shoot is the efficiency unlock — 20 testable combos from one shoot, judged on hook retention first and spend-vs-CPA second.
sequencing: The separation rule (hooks vs bodies, pre-shoot)
The launch size (3–5 per ad group)
The winner rule (don't touch until fatigue)
why_it_works: "Separate hooks from bodies before shooting anything" reframes testing from a filming problem into a planning problem — the combo math (20 from 1 shoot) makes the efficiency visceral.
what_to_steal: LC's shoot planning: every LC video shoot produces hooks and bodies as separable assets (10 hooks × 2 bodies); judge on 5-second retention before ROAS.

product: commentary — no product (breaks down an unnamed app's AI-video scale play)
hook: "no F*CKING way this app scaled from $1k to $500k off ai videos" — disbelief at the numbers.
body: An app scaled $1K → $500K on AI videos of animals/characters doing millions of views; the format: the character performs on camera, the app appears only in captions ("not trying to sell hard"); the remix engine: "swap the hook, swap the character, swap the caption" → 50 tests in an afternoon, no camera touched; most die quietly (expected); you're fishing for the 2–3 that convert; once found, the bottleneck is manpower — creator campaigns solve distribution.
idea: The swap-everything remix engine: hook × character × caption = 50 afternoon tests; the job isn't finding 1,000 formats, it's fishing for the 2–3 converters.
sequencing: The format (character performs, app in captions)
why_it_works: "50 tests in an afternoon" + "most die quietly" gives permission to fail fast — it reframes the 47 dead tests as the cost of finding the 3 winners, not as waste.
what_to_steal: LC's AI-character remix lane: swap hook × avatar × caption across LC jewelry concepts; expect most to die, fish for the 2–3 converters.

product: commentary — no product (the 3-layer remix system post)
hook: "Most brands have a winning ad they haven't made yet and the footage is already sitting on a hard drive." — reframe opener.
body: The 3-layer model: Angle (emotional reason to buy) / Format (UGC, static, podcast, meme) / Execution (creator, hook, script, pacing); when an ad dies it's almost never the angle — it's execution (stale hook, overexposed creator); the rebuild playbook, cheapest first: (1) remix the winning ad — same script new creator, green-screen reaction, swap the hook ("highest leverage move"), franken-cut two winners; (2) same angle, new format — claim becomes bold-text static, podcast clip, B-roll + AI voiceover; (3) winning format, new angle — same energy pointed at a new person, angle pulled from reviews/tickets/surveys; two system rules: set a trigger (frequency >2.5 + declining CTR = iterate now) and never run one variant alone (rotate 4–6 live iterations per winner); the diagnostic question: "which layer is tired?"
idea: "Which layer is tired?" — diagnose the dead ad by layer (angle/format/execution) and rebuild only the cheap tired layer, keeping the proven expensive one.
sequencing: The reframe (winner already on the hard drive)
The rebuild ladder, cheapest first (remix → new format → new angle)
The 4 remix moves (new creator, green-screen, hook swap, franken-cut)
The format swaps (static, podcast, B-roll + AI VO)
formatting: Long text post; the folder's deepest playbook.
why_it_works: "Which layer is tired?" turns ad death from a mystery into a triage question — and "rebuild the cheap layer, keep the expensive one" is the most capital-efficient creative doctrine in the folder.
what_to_steal: LC's full remix SOP: every LC winner gets the 3-layer diagnosis on death; hook-swap first (highest leverage), 4–6 live iterations rotating, trigger at frequency >2.5 + declining CTR.
